A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OminiControl and contain readable main text and complete supplementary material. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching the equations, tables, figures and appendix results across their reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original spatially aligned generation experiments, subject-driven evaluations, ablations and a user study with 375 valid responses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, evaluation metrics and component ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains VAE and DiT reuse, LoRA adaptation, concatenated condition tokens, task-dependent position offsets and attention-bias strength control. Expanded explanations and reordered token notation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v5 Figure S6(c) adds reference-face identity preservation examples involving a human and an illustrated character. This modestly extends the represented inputs beyond the earlier object and clothing examples. The training datasets, COCO evaluation, DreamBooth benchmark and spatial tasks remain.

E2.justification: v5 Table 2 adds FLUX.1 Tools comparisons for Canny, depth and masking. Figure S6 additionally evaluates FR Inversion (as labeled), BlipDiffusion and FastComposer on subject-driven generation, and InstantID on face identity preservation. These additions substantially broaden the quantitative and qualitative comparator set; the earlier principal baselines remain.

E3.justification: v5 adds CLIP-IQA, PSNR and CLIP Image metrics to spatial evaluation; CLIP Text corresponds to the earlier CLIP-Score. Figure 10 introduces component-specific LoRA removal controls. The stated datasets, resolutions, sample counts, base models and principal training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds qualitative ablations removing LoRA from normalization, MLP, output and attention projections in Figure 10. Figure 5 supplements the existing position-indexing analysis with outputs after 15,000 iterations. The earlier training-data ablation is retained in Appendix B.1/Figure S4, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed average and best-score reporting for subject-driven evaluation, the fixed spatial-evaluation seed and the same shaded training-loss plots. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or changed repeated-run procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The spatial-results table is extensively revised and expanded. OminiControl's reported Canny F1 changes from 0.38 to 0.50, while FID changes from 20.63 to 24.20; depth MSE changes from 903 to 537. New metrics, comparator scores and qualitative results are added. Table 3 and subject-driven Table S1 remain unchanged. These are reported result changes, without an established explanation for the revisions.

T1.justification: The intended attention mathematics is retained, but v5 introduces a localized defect in Equation 6. Tokens are reordered to X, CT, CI, with lengths N, M, N, while several bias-matrix blocks retain incompatible dimensions, including an M-by-M top-left block. v4's corresponding block dimensions were consistent. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central parameter-efficiency, universal-control and Subjects200K claims remain. v5 promotes inference-time attention-bias control to an explicit contribution, including adjustment 'without compromising performance.' Its conclusion also replaces v4's scalability assertion with effectiveness across aligned and non-aligned tasks.

C2.justification: v5 newly acknowledges that additional tokens can limit inference efficiency. It also interprets the component ablations as suggesting that control propagates through normalization and attention routing, with query/key adaptation more consequential than value adaptation. These add substantive qualifications and mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: v5 supplies a concrete example positional offset, (0,32), and the prompt used for the attention visualization. It removes v4's direct OminiControl repository link, while retaining the Subjects200K link in Appendix A. The principal optimizer, hardware, training and dataset-generation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands substantially. New Section 3.2.4 positions OminiControl against ACE, ACE++, FLUX and task-specific concurrent approaches. Paired-image synthesis now acknowledges Group Diffusion Transformers and In-context LoRA. Numerous additional conditioning works are cited, while v4's MM-Diffusion reference is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction and method narrative are rewritten. Section 3.2 gains explicit subsections organizing architecture, token interactions, flexible control and concurrent work. Experimental exposition is reorganized, and the training-data analysis moves to the supplement.

P2.justification: v4 Figures 2–3 are merged and redrawn as v5 Figure 2. The main results table is expanded and reformatted, Figure 7 is redesigned, and its full spatial comparison is retained in Figure S6(a). New ablation and comparison panels are added, the dataset montage is condensed, and the conditioning-strength figure receives a corrected caption.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons, component ablations and explicit inference-cost limitation strengthen evaluation and qualification of the claims. However, v4's deblurring FID claim of 30.38 to 11.49 matched its table; v5 retains that claim although Table 2 reports 16.27 to 18.89, reversing the comparison. Together with the newly inconsistent dimensions in Equation 6, these reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
